newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel to free Palestinian women prisoners.
newsitem.headline: Israel to free Palestinian women prisoners.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Friday that all female Palestinian prisoners held by Israel would be freed, fulfilling a commitment made in an interim peace deal with the PLO.
"The prime minister reported to the government ministers that an order was given to free the Palestinian female prisoners," the cabinet statement said.
It gave no date for the release, however, and Netanyahu's spokesmen were not immediately available to comment.

Israel Radio said the release would occur next week because President Ezer Weizman had to pardon several of the prisoners before they could be freed and that process would hold up the release until next week.

Weizman had previously refused to pardon some of the prisoners. The prisoners he had pardoned then refused to go free if their comrades could not. The cabinet statement said the president had now decided to pardon all of them.
Only 25 of the nearly 5,000 Palestinian prisoners held by Israel are women.
Netanyahu, who ousted Israel's previous government in elections last May, has said he will honour all commitments signed by that government. The prisoner release is one of those commitments.

In a deal with the Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) in January under which Israeli troops withdrew from 80 percent of the West Bank town of Hebron, also fulfilling an accord signed by the prior government, Netanyahu pledged to carry out the prisoner release.
